column3: “Some men” supplies the subject; “son” specifies child.
“Matthew” makes the final subject explicit; the historical present becomes past.
“Matthew’s” identifies the house without an explicit possessive in the Greek.
“Jesus” makes the pronoun explicit; the historical present becomes past.
“Guests of the bridegroom” interprets sons of the bridal chamber; “time” replaces days.
“Jesus” and “the girl” make the pronouns explicit; the passive raising becomes getting up.
